keybinds: key.vanillaplusadditions.arm_target_overlay.peek_modifier - en_us "Show Mechanical Arm Targets (hold + look at arm)", de_de "Arm-Zielpunkte anzeigen (halten + auf Arm schauen)"; default GLFW_KEY_LEFT_CONTROL (InputConstants.Type.KEYSYM), category key.categories.vanillaplusadditions ("Vanilla+ Additions"); hold-to-peek, rebindable to any key or mouse button. Shares its default key with four other VPA keybinds (see notes).
oneLiner: Hold Left Ctrl while wearing goggles and looking at a Create Mechanical Arm to see glowing boxes around every block it takes from (orange) and deposits into (teal) - even through walls.

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Supplies the Mechanical Arm itself plus Engineering Goggles detection (GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles) and the ArmBlockEntity/ArmInteractionPoint types the overlay reads. Without Create the render handler returns on its first statement, so the module still loads, still initializes and still has its config section and its keybind - it just never draws anything. It is listed as type="optional" in the bundle's mods.toml, and the module does NOT override shouldInitialize().

Create: Aeronautics' aviator's goggles (aeronautics:aviators_goggles) are listed in the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles item tag, so they also unlock the overlay when worn in the vanilla HEAD slot. The tag entry is "required": false, so nothing breaks without the mod; without it only Create's Engineering Goggles work. NOTE: aeronautics is NOT declared as a dependency in neoforge.mods.toml at all - the coupling is the tag entry alone.
optionalMods.evidence: src/main/resources/data/vanillaplusadditions/tags/item/arm_goggles.json:4; absence verified by grep of modId= in src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml (only create, toughasnails, sable, bluemap, neoforge, minecraft)

optionalMods.whatItAdds: Indirect and Create-owned: with Curios installed, Create itself registers a predicate in GogglesItem.IS_WEARING_PREDICATES, so Engineering Goggles worn in a Curios head slot also count. This module writes no Curios code, imports no Curios type and declares no Curios dependency anywhere - it merely inherits the behaviour of the GogglesItem call. Without Curios the goggles must sit in the vanilla helmet slot. The Curios path applies ONLY to Create's own goggles - tag-based goggles (aviator's) are checked strictly in EquipmentSlot.HEAD.

shortDescription: Shows Mechanical Arm input/output positions when wearing Engineering Goggles
notes:
DOC/README CONTRADICTION (most important for a doc writer): both README.md:170 and docs/modules/arm_target_overlay.md:23 say the overlay shows "While wearing Engineering Goggles" / "While wearing compatible goggles and looking directly at a placed Mechanical Arm" - neither mentions that since commit ec47f31 (2026-07-05, beta.30) the overlay ALSO requires the hold-to-peek modifier key (default Left Ctrl) to be physically held. Goggles + looking at the arm alone show nothing (ArmTargetOverlayClientEvents.java:91). The module doc has no keybind section at all; the mapping exists in the code (ArmTargetOverlayKeybinds.java:23-27) and in lang/en_us.json:139 + lang/de_de.json:139, nowhere in prose docs.

SECOND DOC INACCURACY: docs/modules/arm_target_overlay.md:14-15 says goggles work "worn in the head slot (or a Curios slot, if supported by the item)" for the whole arm_goggles tag. In code only Create's own GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles() covers Curios slots (via Create's own predicate registry); the tag check is hard-wired to EquipmentSlot.HEAD (ArmTargetOverlayClientEvents.java:140). Aviator's goggles in a Curios slot do NOT work. Also a naming mismatch: the doc calls them "Aviation Goggles", the tag entry is "aeronautics:aviators_goggles".

README LINK - REPO-WIDE, NOT MODULE-SPECIFIC (correction of the first fact sheet, which framed this as this module's link lagging): README.md:297 links docs/arm_target_overlay.md while the file now lives at docs/modules/arm_target_overlay.md (staged rename in the working tree). This is not specific to this module - 15 of the 16 module links in the README's Documentation section still point at the old flat docs/<name>.md paths; only docs/guides/* links were updated. A doc writer should fix them as one batch, not as an arm_target_overlay item.

README DOES cover the optional-Create side elsewhere: README.md:223 has a table row "| `arm_target_overlay` | Create | Overlay inactive (it visualizes Create's Mechanical Arm targets) |". Note the deliberate contrast with the next row, item_vault_viewer, which reads "Module skips initialization entirely" - that is exactly the shouldInitialize() distinction: this module does NOT gate initialization, it only goes inert.

TRIGGER CHAIN, in order (ArmTargetOverlayClientEvents.onRenderLevelStage, lines 70-109): Create loaded (static CREATE_LOADED, line 63) -> stage == AFTER_TRANSLUCENT_BLOCKS -> module non-null and enabled -> level/player non-null -> goggles worn -> modifier key held -> crosshair hitResult is a BlockHitResult whose block entity is an ArmBlockEntity -> at least one input or output configured. Only ONE arm at a time is drawn: the one the player is directly looking at, within normal reach (minecraft.hitResult). There is no radius, no toggle, no "show all arms" mode.

RENDERING: a custom RenderType "arm_target_overlay_xray_lines" (ArmTargetOverlayClientEvents.java:44-59), DefaultVertexFormat.POSITION_COLOR_NORMAL, VertexFormat.Mode.LINES, buffer size 1536, with RENDERTYPE_LINES_SHADER, VIEW_OFFSET_Z_LAYERING, TRANSLUCENT_TRANSPARENCY, ITEM_ENTITY_TARGET output, COLOR_WRITE write mask, NO_DEPTH_TEST and NO_CULL. NO_DEPTH_TEST is what makes the outlines visible through solid blocks. Line width is OptionalDouble.empty() (vanilla default) and is NOT configurable; only the eight RGBA channels are. Boxes are drawn with LevelRenderer.renderLineBox over new AABB(point.getPos()), i.e. exactly one full block per interaction point.

REFLECTION, NOT MIXIN: ArmBlockEntity.inputs/outputs are package-private in Create and are read via cached reflection (ArmBlockEntityReflection.java, fields resolved once under a synchronized block). A Mixin @Accessor was deliberately rejected because ArmBlockEntity's supertype SmartBlockEntity implements net.createmod.ponder.api.VirtualBlockEntity, which is not in libs/ - see docs/internal/arm_target_overlay_case_study.md (Entscheidung 2). If a future Create version renames those fields, the module fails soft: warnOnce() logs ONE warning via Vpa.LOGGER.warn and the getters return Collections.emptyList() forever after, so the overlay silently draws nothing. There is no user-visible error.

CONFIG LIVES IN THE COMMON SPEC: the eight color keys are registered through AbstractModuleConfig into the COMMON ModConfigSpec (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131 for the bundle, StandaloneModuleBootstrap.java:45 for the standalone jar), even though the feature is 100% client-side. Players edit them in vanillaplusadditions-common.toml (bundle) or vpa_arm_target_overlay-common.toml (standalone); a dedicated server holds the same keys and they do nothing there.

KEYBIND IS ALWAYS REGISTERED: ArmTargetOverlayKeybinds subscribes to RegisterKeyMappingsEvent on the MOD bus (Dist.CLIENT) with no module-enabled and no Create check, so "Show Mechanical Arm Targets" appears in the Controls screen even when the module is disabled in config or Create is absent. isModifierDown() reads raw GLFW window state (InputConstants.isKeyDown / glfwGetMouseButton), not KeyMapping.isDown(), and supports KEYSYM and MOUSE bindings; an UNKNOWN/unbound key returns false (overlay then never shows).

KEYBIND CONFLICT OUT OF THE BOX (missed by the first fact sheet): five VPA key mappings all default to GLFW_KEY_LEFT_CONTROL in the same category key.categories.vanillaplusadditions - arm_target_overlay, item_vault_viewer, cat_guardian, axolotl_guardian and wolf_mount. Minecraft's Controls screen therefore flags them as conflicting on a fresh install. They are separate KeyMapping objects (this module's is ArmTargetOverlayKeybinds.PEEK_MODIFIER), each read independently via raw GLFW state, so the conflict is cosmetic and all of them still work while Ctrl is held - but a doc writer should say so, because the orange conflict marker invites players to rebind.

NO MIXINS, NO SERVER CODE, NO NETWORK, NO REGISTRIES: mixin/arm_target_overlay/ does not exist, vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json has no entry for this module, and build.gradle's standalone descriptor (build.gradle:387-388) lists no mixins. A grep over the module directory finds no DeferredRegister, no command registration, no payload/packet code and exactly two @SubscribeEvent methods. ArmTargetOverlayModule.onInitialize() only logs one line - all behaviour sits in the two @EventBusSubscriber(Dist.CLIENT) classes.

SHARED TAG COUPLING: the vanillaplusadditions:arm_goggles tag is also read by the debug_overlay module (modules/debug_overlay/client/GogglesUtil.java:21-36), which duplicates the same goggles logic instead of reusing this module's private helper. In build.gradle the tag file is shipped only in the arm_target_overlay standalone jar's dataGlobs (build.gradle:388); the debug_overlay standalone entry (build.gradle:420) has no dataGlobs, and coreJar ships only assets/vanillaplusadditions/** (build.gradle:617), no data/** - so a vpa_debug_overlay jar installed without vpa_arm_target_overlay has no arm_goggles tag content to match against. Unlike this module, GogglesUtil guards its GogglesItem call with its own CREATE_LOADED flag; this module's isWearingGoggles() is unguarded and relies entirely on the caller's early return at line 70.

STANDALONE JAR: entrypoint class src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/standalone/arm_target_overlay/ArmTargetOverlayStandalone.java (@Mod("vpa_arm_target_overlay"), line 13) hands the module to StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot(). The generated mods.toml (renderModuleToml, build.gradle:507-535) declares only vpa_core, neoforge and minecraft as required plus the bundle "vanillaplusadditions" as incompatible - it declares NO create dependency at all, not even optional, and therefore no ordering="AFTER" create. Only the bundle jar declares create optional with ordering="AFTER" (neoforge.mods.toml:82-87).

sinceVersion CAVEAT (re-verified): the commit that added the module directory on the current master is b79951d (2026-06-09, "release: v0.17.0 - Arm Target Overlay module"). `git tag --contains b79951d` reports v0.18.0 as the earliest tag, because the history was rewritten: tag v0.17.0 points at 3f503f4, a twin commit with the identical subject and date that is NOT an ancestor of master (`git merge-base --is-ancestor v0.17.0 master` -> false). The v0.17.0 tree does contain all four module source files and v0.16.0 contains none of them (verified with `git ls-tree -r --name-only`), so the module shipped in v0.17.0.
